The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2136 of 2014
Judgment:

Challenging the order and decree, dated 30.09.2013 passed in M.V.O.P.No.892 of 2011 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge,
Warangal (for short "the Tribunal"), in partly allowing the claim-petition, the present appeal is filed by the Insurance Company.

entities.text:
Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge,
Warangal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For convenience, the parties are hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 27.05.2011, one Utukuri Venkataiah (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased') and his family members engaged an auto bearing No.AP 36 V 2393, insured with respondent No.2, owned by respondent No.1, to attend marriage at Veerannapet village.
At about 02.00 p.m., when the deceased reached outskirts of Musthyala village, the driver of the said auto drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the said auto turned turtle.
As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Area Hospital,
Cherial.
Later, he was shifted to Care Hospital, Hyderabad and thereafter, he took treatment at Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad.

entities.text: Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On 05.06.2011, at about 09:30 a.m., the LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 deceased succumbed to the injuries while undergoing treatment.

The Claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- for the death of the deceased i.e., Utukuri Venkataiah, husband of claimant No.1,
father of claimant Nos.2 to 4, who died in a vehicle accident that occurred on 27.05.2011.

According to the claimants, the deceased was aged about 45 years and earning Rs.6,000/- per month as an agriculturist and toddy tapper and used to contribute his entire earnings for the welfare of the family.
Due to his sudden demise, the claimants lost their bread winner, love and affection.
Therefore, they filed the O.P. claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- lakh against the respondents.

4. Before the Tribunal, the respondent No. 1, owner, filed counter stating that the said auto is insured with respondent No.2 and the same is in force at the time of accident and as such,
respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and prayed to dismiss the appeal against him.
On other hand, respondent No.2-insurance company, filed counter denying the manner in which the accident took place, including the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
It is also stated that the quantum of compensation claimed is excessive, baseless and prayed to dismiss the petition.
LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 5.

Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:

1

entities.text: United India Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Utukuri Balavva, Warangal Dist And 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Whether the accident occurred on 27.05.2011 at about 14:00 hours at the outskirts of Musthyala village, Cherial Mandal, Warangal District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto bearing No. AP 36 V 2393?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. To what relief?
6.
In order to prove the issues, PWs.1 & 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A6 got marked on behalf of the claimants.
On behalf of respondents, RW.1 was examined and Exs.B1 to B5 were marked.
On behalf of Tribunal, Ex.X1 was marked.

7. Considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Tribunal has partly allowed O.P. awarding compensation of Rs.5,30,343/- with interest at 7% per annum payable by respondent No.2 at the first instance and therafter, recover the same from respondent No.1.
Challenging the same, the present appeal has been filed by the respondent No.2/Insurance company.
8. Heard Sri M.Rama Krishna, learned Standing Counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and Sri Ajay Kumar Madisetty, learned counsel for claimants.
Perused the record.
LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 9.
The learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company contended that though there is a delay of 10 days in filing the FIR, the Tribunal has erroneously allowed the O.P.
He further contended that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation as the driver of the said auto was not having valid driving licence on the date of accident.
Hence, he prayed to allow the appeal.
10. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimants contended that the claim petition cannot be rejected simply on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
In this regard, he placed reliance on the Judgement of the Apex Court in Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others 1.

He further contended that by following the judgment of the Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. V.
Swaran Singh and others 2, the Tribunal has rightly directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation at first instance and then recover the same from the owner of the said auto, which needs no interference by this Court.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd. V.
Swaran Singh and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he prayed to dismiss the appeal.

11. Coming to the aspect of 10 days delay in lodging the compliant, the Apex Court in case of Ravi (Supra 1), observed that 2011 (4) SCC 693 (2004) 3 SCC 297 LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 "although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.

Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are United India Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Utukuri Balavva, Warangal Dist And 4 ... on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166777767/
2 composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Utukuri Balavva, Warangal Dist And 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

This Court, having respectful agreement with the view taken by the Apex Court in the aforesaid judgment, is of the considered opinion that mere delay in filing FIR is not sufficient to defeat the claim petition.

12. As regards the aspect of liability of payment of compensation, as per the evidence of RW.1,
neither the driving licence of the driver of the said auto nor RC, permit and fitness certificate was filed.
He also deposed that respondent No.1 permitted his driver even after knowing that he does not possess the valid driving licence, to drive the said auto.

Thus, there is breach of terms and conditions on the part of the owner of the offending vehicle as he had entrusted the vehicle to a person, who was not holding valid driving licence by the time of accident.
The LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 fact remains that by the time of accident, the offending vehicle was insured with the appellant and Ex.B.1 policy was very much in force.

In case of third party risks, as per the decision in Swaran Singh (Supra 2), the insurer had to indemnify the compensation amount payable to the third party and the insurance company may recover the same from the insured.

In the said decision, the Apex Court considered the doctrine of "pay and recover" examined the liability of the insurance company in cases of breach of policy condition due to disqualifications of the driver or invalid driving license of the driver and held that in case of third party risks, the insurer has to indemnify the compensation amount to the third party and the insurance company may recover the same from the insured.

Recently, the Apex Court in Shamanna v. The Divisional Manager, the Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others 3, following its earlier decision in Swaran Singh (Supra 2), reiterated that "even if the driver does not possess any driving license, still the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and that he can recover the award amount from the owner of the offending vehicle after paying the amount."

entities.text: Shamanna v. The Divisional Manager, the Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the Tribunal has rightly directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount at the first instance and then recover 2018 ACJ 2163 LNA, J Macma_2136_2014 the same from the owner of the vehicle by invoking the doctrine of pay and recover.

13. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, considering the evidence and duly taking into consideration the age of the deceased, the Tribunal has awarded the total compensation of Rs.5,30,343/- which cannot be said to be on higher side.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the award passed by the Tribunal and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
14. Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A. is dismissed confirming the award and decree passed by the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
